intro: The Tier 1 SSC CGL exam held on 11 October 2026 showed a range of difficulty levels across its three shifts. Shift 1 was described as Easy to Moderate, while Shifts 2 and 3 were largely reported as Easy. Good attempts were noted around 17‑18 questions for Shift 1; attempts for the other shifts were not reliably reported. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as Easy to Moderate, whereas Shifts 2 and 3 were mostly described as Easy. The overall perception therefore ranged from Easy to Moderate on that date.

faqs.q: How many questions were considered well‑attempted in Shift 1 on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 reports indicated that candidates attempted about 17 to 18 questions well. This number is based on unofficial summaries.

faqs.q: What were the section‑wise difficulty trends for the exam on 11 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, reasoning was Easy to Moderate, General Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude showed mixed difficulty, and English was Moderate. Shifts 2 and 3 had all four sections – reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude and English – reported as Easy.

faqs.q: Are the average marks reported for Shift 2 on 11 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No. The average marks for Shift 2 (ranging from 26.56 to 41.59 per section and a total of 137.21) come from partial reports and are not official figures.

faqs.q: How does SSC normalise scores across shifts for the 11 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC applies a standardisation process that adjusts raw scores from each shift to a common scale, allowing candidates from different shifts to be compared fairly. The exact formula is not publicly disclosed.
